pr_title: Don't remove trailing `\0` in custom attributes
pr_body: As the comment says - this behavior goes against the spec. Fixes #49756.

issue_context.title: Custom attributes that have strings ending in 0 don't roundtrip
comments:
/cc @jaredpar

Not sure what was the legacy compiler compat reason that lead to adding this. 

I think it would make sense to remove the trimming from `BlobReader.ReadSerializedString` in .NET 6 and add it to Roslyn instead. Or perhaps even remove it from Roslyn?

It'd be a breaking change but it doesn't seem like a significant one - `\0` can still be returned if it is in the middle of the string the caller must be able to handle strings with `\0` anyways.

@AlekseyTs do you know of any specific cases that drove this compat quirk? 

If not I think we could consider fixing for .NET 6. As @tmat mentioned if we find a real case that drove this we could consider putting the patch in the roslyn code base.
I do not know the specific case, but probably changing the behavior will break some unit-test with specific scenario.
Native compilers behavior was probably caused by the fact that C++ strings are null-terminated and everything after `\0` was ignored.

Actually - does Roslyn depend on this at all? This appears to be used in two spots: `ReadSerializedString`, the public API, and as an implementation detail of the custom attribute decoder.

I found some instances of `ReadSerializedString` in the Roslyn repo that appear to be test-only. Then I searched for `ICustomAttributeTypeProvider` that would indicate the attribute decoder is being used, and found nothing? Could it be that this has no impact on Roslyn?

If so, https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/50088 should be hopefully a trivial review.

review_comments: Were there any tests for this that need to be deleted?  Or any we want to add to ensure we're not trimming these?

We'll see in the CI and I'll delete as needed.

I thought about adding a test, but do we also want to test that we don't trim after `\0` in the middle of the string or at the beginning then? (I'm not sure a test for this has a leg to stand on if we forget about the history of this - we don't generally test "absence of logic in the product that breaks stuff".

> I'm not sure a test for this has a leg to stand on if we forget about the history of this

A comment can ensure we don't forget about the history :)

But I don't feel strongly about it.  I'm generally just questioning of any change that impacts product behavior and has zero test impact.

>return ReadUTF8(length); [](start = 16, length = 24)

Are we certain this change affects exclusively custom attributes and nothing else?

> Are we certain this change affects exclusively custom attributes and nothing else?

Well `BlobReader.ReadSerializedString` is a public API so people can use it for all sorts of stuff; the internal usage is confined to custom attributes. The null-trimming behavior was not documented and after this change, the implementation is going to match [the docs](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.reflection.metadata.blobreader.readserializedstring?view=net-5.0) (that simply refers to ECMA-335 for the semantic).

> Well BlobReader.ReadSerializedString is a public API so people can use it for all sorts of stuff; the internal usage is confined to custom attributes. 

Perhaps the title of the commit should have reflected the actual impact of the change then.
